messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I'm still looking for precisions about these questions, down the mail, 
about the embeding of iPlots, maybe someone have an idea ?

I would like to ask too whether it would be possible to have a small 
working Java test case for the BarCanvas?
I tried some things but got some errors or infinite loops, here is my 
last test:

public class TestMain extends Frame {

     public TestMain() {
         this.setMinimumSize(new Dimension(400,  400));
         this.setVisible(true);

         SVarFact associatedVariable =  new SVarFact("test", new 
int[]{1, 2, 3, 4}, new String[]{"cat1", "cat2", "cat3", "cat4"});
         associatedVariable.createMissingsCat();

         SMarker associatedMarker = new SMarker(4);

         BarCanvas b = new BarCanvas(0, this, associatedVariable, 
associatedMarker); // 0 for AWTGraphicDevice
         this.pack();

     }

     public static void main(String[] args) {
         new TestMain();
     }
}

I got no errors or infinite loops but nothing is drawn in the Frame, 
maybe I need to call some repaint method or add a repaint listener 
anywhere ?
Thanks in advance.
Sebastian


Le 13/09/2013 16:01, Centre Jacques-Petit a écrit :
>
> Le 12/09/2013 18:03, Simon Urbanek a écrit :
>> On Sep 12, 2013, at 11:20 AM, Centre Jacques-Petit wrote:
>>
>>> Le 12/09/2013 15:33, Simon Urbanek a écrit :
>>>> Sebastian,
>>>>
>>>> On Sep 12, 2013, at 3:28 AM, Centre Jacques-Petit wrote:
>>>>
>>>>> Hello,
>>>>> in a Java SWT application, we need to add semantic data to some 
>>>>> plots generated by R. At the moment, we're looking at the iPlots 
>>>>> package and at the possiblity to embed it in the application.
>>>>>
>>>>> The toolkit doesn't seem to offer all the functions for our needs. 
>>>>> We need to, for example, create new graph types, add custom Java 
>>>>> GUI components (as menus, tooltips, translate the entries if we 
>>>>> keep some of existent ones, etc.) and to capture/add custom Java 
>>>>> events from the iPlots Window/Canvas components (eg. bars, points 
>>>>> of scatters, etc.).
>>>>> After some research, it appears the better way could be to modify 
>>>>> the Java source code of the iplots.jar package if we want to do 
>>>>> this (I think extend it may not be enough for our needs).
>>>>>
>>>> Your statements are somewhat surprising. iPlots have been designed 
>>>> specifically to allow very easy ways to extend it and create new 
>>>> plot types. The framework is highly modular, new plot types are 
>>>> easy to create (have a look at the icp package that even allows you 
>>>> to do that direct from R without any Java code) and new primitives 
>>>> can be added by simple subclassing. I would recommend familiarizing 
>>>> yourself with the design of the framework if possible (probably the 
>>>> most extensive description is in Chapter 4 of "Exploratory Model 
>>>> Analysis: An Interactive Graphical Framework for Model Comparison 
>>>> and Selection", more recent overview if iPlots eXtreme which holds 
>>>> true for the most part for the older iPlots as well is in the 
>>>> iPlots eXtreme DSC paper http://urbanek.info/pub/dsc09.pdf ). Let 
>>>> me know if you have any questions, I'd be happy to help.
>>> Thank you very much for these precisions and this document, I'll 
>>> read it carefully.
>>> Indeed, I have not yet understood well how the toolkit works. I will 
>>> test the framework and look at the icp package, I didn't know it.
>>> Is there any other developper document or a javadoc you could advise 
>>> to me for understanding the Java iplots.jar package ?
>>
>> http://rforge.net/org/docs/
>>
> Thanks for this Javadoc. I'll try the inheritage approach.
>>>>> Could you tell us if the Java source code is distributed and if 
>>>>> so, under which license ? (the Java source code is not on Cran)
>>>>>
>>>> The sources are available under GPLv2 (see the package).
>>>> http://www.rforge.net/iplots/svn.html
>>> Thank you, I'll check the svn.
>>>>> If the licence is compatible, do you think is it possible to embed 
>>>>> iPlots in an other Java application in easy way ? iPlot seems to 
>>>>> run his own JVM inside R process and I guess it'll may be 
>>>>> difficult to embed the iPlots canvas in existent Java GUI 
>>>>> components in already run Java application.
>>>>>
>>>> Not at all - see JGR - it embeds both R and iPlots into a Java 
>>>> application.
>>> Actually, I thought R was loading JGR (through rJava). Do you mean 
>>> that it's JGR (Java side) which launches R when you use the 
>>> jgrLaunch.bat script ?
>> No, JGR is a Java application that loads R (via JRI). R can call back 
>> into that app using rJava.
> OK, I concluded this because I saw that we could launch JGR() from an 
> R console but now I realise a JGR() call simply run a new JGR/R and 
> give back hand to the first process (the 2 process seem to be separated).
>
>>
>>> The other point I didn't understand is how JGR uses iPlots. When you 
>>> call an iPlots function through the JGR console I thought the iPlots 
>>> Java classes was call through R/rJava, is it wrong ?
>> Yes, that is correct, but it's the same JVM that the JGR app runs in, 
>> so it can call the Java classes directly without R. R is just used to 
>> supply the data, you can simply create the data in Java instead as 
>> SVar are just Java classes anyway.
> Ok, so it's the same JVM, thanks.
>>
>>> That's why I thought that iPlots wasn't embedded in JGR but launched 
>>> by R, was I wrong ?
>>>>   If you wanted, you could do even without the R process since 
>>>> iPlots use it only for R-side extensibility.
>>> There's another point I don't understand well, if we want to add 
>>> iPlots Java components to a Java application, how the link between R 
>>> and iPlots can be done ?
>> JRI - see above - but it is purely optional
> OK.
>>
>>> Does iPlots need to be launched by rJava or iPlots can launch R (or 
>>> iPlots can communicate with an R session already launched by the 
>>> Java application) ?
>>>
>>> Our Java application works through RServe and launches it at start 
>>> so I think, as is, it's not compatible with the embedding of iPlots 
>>> in the Java GUI but I need to do more research on this point (and 
>>> that's another question).
>>>
>> Again, you don't care for iPlots. The iPlots classes work entirely in 
>> Java, the interactivity is implemented on the Java side - the R 
>> communication is optional if you want R callbacks, but you don't have 
>> to use them.
>>
>>
> So if I understand well, for communicate between R, iPlots and the SWT 
> Java application and for embed an iPlots Canvas in the GUI we can :
> - continue using Rserve, create our own Java data set and give it to 
> iPlots Java
> (it means we have to embed the Canvas to the GUI using Java and we 
> have to add the custom events and custom widgets using Java)
> - launch R through JRI within the Java application and run iPlots in R

> - the solution above could work too, in same way, by launching our

>
> I'd have another question, could you please confirm me what I think

Joe Byers <ecjbosu <at> aim.com> writes:

> 
> 
> I am trying to get rJava to load the htmlunit java package
> (http://htmlunit.sourceforge.net/).  rJava
> does not seem to be able to load and find the class in this package.  This
> issue is the same on Windows 7 and
> Fedora 17 computers.
> 
> rJava will load and init because I can see java.util.* classes, java.net.*
> classes,
> java.io.IOException, and cssparser classes.  cssparser is required by
htmlunit.
> 
> Thanks for you help.
> Joe W. Byers
> 

> 
> 

All,

I finally figure out how to get rJava to recognize the htmlunit classes. 
This required loading all the jar dependency files in the htmlunit binary
zip file on the java class path in rJava.  On windows or Fedora 16 or less,
it is simply copying the jars to a special directory and executing
.jaddClassPath.  On linux Fedora 17 or greate, it will require executing
.jaddClassPath on all the jar files in the /usr/share/java directory that
are require by htmlunit.  I wrote a special function that I need to add to
my startup sources before calling rJava that will load all jars that I need
on my classpath.  

The method is 
setJarClasses <-function (jardir='c:/libraries/jar'){
require(rJava);

.jinit()
#load jars

#jar directory
#put in a system cache database
jarfiles = list.files(jardir, all.files = F, full.names = T, include.dirs=F);


ret=lapply(jarfiles, function(x) .jaddClassPath(x));

}   


The call is 
serJarClasses('/usr/share/java') #or other directory.  

Changing this method to accept a list of file names as well would improve it.

messages.body_plain:
Thank you for your help Simon,
I confirm it was my mistake using RServe API, I definitely don't need
"pairlists" but simple R lists.
Using RXPGenericVector instead of RList as suggested fix my error.
Best regards,
Fabio

2013/10/18 Simon Urbanek <simon.urbanek at r-project.org>:
> Fabio,
>
> On Oct 17, 2013, at 6:39 AM, Fabio Bucci wrote:
>
>> My goal is to reproduce using the REngine java client the creation of
>> an empty list, like:
>>
>>> a <- list()
>>> is.list(a)
>> [1] TRUE
>>> length(a)
>> [1] 0
>>
>> I've written a simple test to check the behaviour of an empty REXPList object.
>> I've created an empty list as:
>> new REXPList
>>
>
> that is not the equivalent of the above. REXPList is a *pairlist* in R, but list() is a generic vector and thus RXPGenericVector. So the equivalent to
>
> a <- list()
>
> would be
>
> new REXPGenericVector(new RList())
>
> Also note that an empty pairlist is by definition NULL, so there is no way to distinguish NULL from an empty pairlist in R -- see
>> pairlist()
> NULL
>
> Now, unfortunately REngine interface allows the creation of empty pairlists separate from NULL, although they don't exist in R. So the behavior is undefined and each implementation does something different. I suppose the most consistent behavior would be to change JRI implementation to create a NULL object instead - although it doesn't solve the issue of having two Java representations for the same object (REXPNull and REXPList with length 0), at least it doesn't give a misleading result, so I think I'll change that.
>
> Thanks,
> Simon
>
>
>> I'd like to check that:
>> rexp.isList() returns true
>> rexp.asList().size() returns 0
>>
>> then I'd like to assign the variable to an REngine object and read the
>> same variable as a new REXP object, repeating the same tests.
>>
>> Using an RConnection implementation the test succeed, using a JRI
>> implementation the new list's length is equal to 1 (it contains an
>> REXPNull object as first element).
>> Am I missing something? Could be a JRI bug?
>> Is there a way to have a consistent result, not dependent from the
>> REngine implementation?
>>
>> This is the code to replicate my test (needs JUnit 4):
>>
>> import static org.junit.Assert.*;
>>
>> import org.junit.Test;
>> import org.rosuda.REngine.REXP;
>> import org.rosuda.REngine.REXPList;
>> import org.rosuda.REngine.REXPMismatchException;
>> import org.rosuda.REngine.REngine;
>> import org.rosuda.REngine.REngineException;
>> import org.rosuda.REngine.RList;
>> import org.rosuda.REngine.JRI.JRIEngine;
>> import org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RConnection;
>>
>> public class TestEmptyListBehavior {
>>
>> @Test
>> public void testEmptyListRemote() throws REngineException,
>> REXPMismatchException {
>> testEmptyList(new RConnection("localhost", 6700));
>> }
>>
>> @Test
>> public void testEmptyListLocal() throws REngineException,
>> REXPMismatchException {
>> testEmptyList(new JRIEngine());
>> }
>>
>> private void testEmptyList(REngine engine) throws REngineException,
>> REXPMismatchException {
>> REXP emptyList =new REXPList(new RList());
>> assertTrue("is a list?",emptyList.isList());
>> assertEquals("is an empty list?",0,emptyList.asList().size());
>>
>> engine.assign("myEmptyList", emptyList, null);
>>
>> REXP rexp=engine.get("myEmptyList", null, true);
>> assertTrue("is a list?",rexp.isList());
>> assertEquals("is an empty list?",0,rexp.asList().size());
>> }
>>
>> }
>>
>> Many thanks,
>> Fabio
>>
>> _______________________________________________
>> stats-rosuda-devel mailing list
>> stats-rosuda-devel at listserv.uni-augsburg.de
>> http://mailman.rz.uni-augsburg.de/mailman/listinfo/stats-rosuda-devel

messages.body_plain:
On 10/17/2013 02:05 PM, Joe Byers wrote:
> Joe Byers <ecjbosu <at> aim.com> writes:
>
>>
>>
>> I am trying to get rJava to load the htmlunit java package
>> (http://htmlunit.sourceforge.net/).  rJava
>> does not seem to be able to load and find the class in this package.  This
>> issue is the same on Windows 7 and
>> Fedora 17 computers.
>>
>> rJava will load and init because I can see java.util.* classes, java.net.*
>> classes,
>> java.io.IOException, and cssparser classes.  cssparser is required by
> htmlunit.
>>
>> Thanks for you help.
>> Joe W. Byers
>>
>
>>
>>
>
> All,
>
> I finally figure out how to get rJava to recognize the htmlunit classes.
> This required loading all the jar dependency files in the htmlunit binary
> zip file on the java class path in rJava.  On windows or Fedora 16 or less,
> it is simply copying the jars to a special directory and executing
> .jaddClassPath.  On linux Fedora 17 or greate, it will require executing
> .jaddClassPath on all the jar files in the /usr/share/java directory that
> are require by htmlunit.  I wrote a special function that I need to add to
> my startup sources before calling rJava that will load all jars that I need
> on my classpath.
>
> The method is
> setJarClasses <-function (jardir='c:/libraries/jar'){
> require(rJava);
>
> .jinit()
> #load jars
>
> #jar directory
> #put in a system cache database
> jarfiles = list.files(jardir, all.files = F, full.names = T, include.dirs=F);
>
>
> ret=lapply(jarfiles, function(x) .jaddClassPath(x));
>
> }
>
>
> The call is
> serJarClasses('/usr/share/java') #or other directory.
>
> Changing this method to accept a list of file names as well would improve it.
>
>
>
>

For linux, Fedora 17 and below, installations there are missing 
dependencies.  The htmlunit-version-bin.zip needs to be installed in a 
directory as was required on a Windows machine.  I used /opt/XXXXX/jars. 
  I then passed this directory to the setJarClasses function that is 
sourced from my Rprofile.site.


Another note.  One can place symbolic links to jar files in 
/usr/share/java in /opt/XXXXX/jars for packages like mysql jdbc, 
javamail, and others that are needed with your rJava programs.

Thank you
